How long will a BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 run a full-size refrigerator? (US 120 V)

Yes, it runs it 15 h

Every check passes: 55 W running against 1,800 W continuous, and 286 W at start-up inside a 3,600 W ceiling. The runtime below applies this load’s 85% duty cycle and the station’s own 10 W idle draw — not a label-wattage guess.

Derived from official coefficients + Derived by WattPair · verified 2026-08-01 · US 120 V unit × full-size refrigerator

Usable capacity 829.4 Wh
Surge headroom 10×+

Two numbers decide this, and readers arrive using them interchangeably. Watts are the ceiling on what the inverter can hold at any instant — a full-size refrigerator needs 55 W of them while it runs, and 286 W for the instant it starts. Watt-hours are how much energy the battery holds, and the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 holds 829.4 Wh of them that are actually retrievable. A machine can have plenty of one and not enough of the other.

The verdict above is a calculation — running watts, start-up inrush, duty cycle and inverter waveform against this machine's continuous output, surge ceiling and a usable-capacity figure derived from BLUETTI's own published coefficients — not a lookup. The hours divide that capacity by the load plus the machine's own idle draw.

Where those numbers come from

Every figure below carries the tier it came from and the date it was checked. A blank is never left blank: a field we have found no figure for says so, and a field whose sources disagree — two documents, or one document with itself — says that instead of picking one.

We have read the maker documentation we could find for this class and come away with no inrush figure, so the multiple this site uses is a category envelope drawn from standards tables. It is deliberately conservative, it is not a measurement of any particular unit, and its confidence is capped accordingly. A verdict held back by this number may well be fine in practice — we will not say so until a manufacturer does.

Questions people ask about this pairing

Will a BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 run a full-size refrigerator?
Yes. 55 W of running draw against 1,800 W of continuous output — 3.1% of it, with 286 W demanded at start-up against a 3,600 W ceiling. The verdict is computed from running watts, start-up inrush and inverter waveform — the working is in the evidence section above.
How long will a BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 run a full-size refrigerator?
About 15 hours on a full charge. That divides a usable-capacity figure derived from BLUETTI's own published depth of discharge and inverter efficiency by this load's duty-weighted draw plus the machine's own 10 W idle draw — not the nameplate watt-hours divided by a label wattage, which is where the confident-looking 20–35% overstatements come from.
Can a BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 run a full-size refrigerator and something else at the same time?
That depends on the something else, and the two numbers to check are on this page. This load takes 55 W of the 1,800 W available, leaving 1,745 W before the 82% line matters, and the start-up headroom is 12.6× — the part people forget, because two motors starting together is a different question from two motors running together. The runtime calculator linked below takes a list of loads rather than one.
